coverage: Weekend edition, week of Nov 23 to 27, with preview of Nov 30 to Dec 4
moodReason: The S&P 500 posted its best week since April 2025 after a sharp correction, with chip and AI stocks leading the rebound. The rally is fragile, though: the Fed is widely expected to raise rates in December, and the Friday jobs report is a major test.

stories.headline: S&P 500 posts its best week since April 2025 as chip and AI stocks rebound
stories.what: The S&P 500 rose 5.6% for the holiday-shortened week, its best week since April 2025, after falling into a correction earlier in the week. All 11 S&P 500 sectors rose on Friday, and the Dow had its biggest weekly gain since October 2022.
stories.why: A broad rebound that starts from a correction can restore buyer confidence, but the size of the move on a thin holiday session also raises the risk of a pullback once full volume returns.

stories.headline: Chip stocks suffer their worst week since 2001 before recovering
stories.what: One market report said the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 17.13% over the period, its worst week since 2001, before investors bought back AI and chip stocks into Friday's rally. Sources differ on the exact size of the drop, so treat the figure as approximate.
stories.why: Semiconductors carry a large share of index weight and of AI-driven earnings expectations. Their swings explain much of the index volatility, so whether the rebound holds depends heavily on this group.

stories.headline: Anthropic completes record IPO, then shares slide
stories.what: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share in what was reported as the largest IPO on record. Shares rose on debut day and then fell, and sources give conflicting figures for the size of the raise and for Friday's move.
stories.why: A record listing absorbs a large amount of investor capital and tests appetite for AI valuations. A weak aftermarket can weigh on sentiment for other AI names and future offerings.

stories.headline: Nvidia beats on revenue and raises outlook, but leadership and regulatory questions linger
stories.what: Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of about $115.8 billion, roughly double a year earlier, with data center revenue up 110% and a raised outlook. Reports on the company's leadership and an SEC investigation were inconsistent across sources, so they are not included here.
stories.why: Nvidia is the largest weight in AI-related equity exposure. Strong results support the AI capital spending thesis, while governance and regulatory uncertainty can cap how far the stock and sector can rally.

stories.headline: Markets price in a December Fed rate hike as core inflation runs above target
stories.what: Futures pricing cited in coverage of the week ahead put the odds of a quarter-point hike at the December 8 to 9 Fed meeting near 98 to 99%. October core PCE rose 3.3% year over year, well above the Fed's 2% target.
stories.why: A tightening move that is already priced in still pressures valuations, especially for long-duration growth stocks and small caps. The bigger risk is a hawkish tone that suggests more hikes ahead.

stories.headline: Treasury yields jumped in mid-November, pressuring stocks and the dollar
stories.what: In the week ended Nov 13, the 10-year Treasury yield rose about 30 basis points to around 5.14%, breaking above 5.00% for the first time since late October. The dollar strengthened to a 2026 high on a more hawkish view of Fed policy.
stories.why: Higher long-term yields raise borrowing costs across the economy and compete with stocks for investor money. This was an important backdrop to the November selloff, and yields need to stabilize for the rebound to last.

watch.item: Fed speakers begin a run of appearances through Dec 4
ISM manufacturing index and JOLTS job openings report
November jobs report, consensus about 90,000 new jobs and 4.1% unemployment
Federal Reserve meeting, with a quarter-point hike widely expected

bottomLine: U.S. stocks ended a volatile holiday week with their best weekly gain in more than a year, led by chips and AI names after a sharp correction. The rebound is real but fragile, because inflation remains well above target and a December rate hike is close to fully priced. The jobs report on Dec 4 and the Fed meeting on Dec 8 to 9 will decide whether the rally holds.
